newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - May 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - May 7.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- BANK GIVEN POWER TO SET BASE RATES

New chancellor Gordon Brown has unveiled the biggest shake- up at the Bank of England since the UK's central bank was nationalised in 1946. Brown announced Tuesday that the power to set base interest rates would be transferred from the Treasury to the Bank of England. The move is designed to reassure markets that political considerations will not be allowed to govern the setting of interest rates.
-- CHANCELLOR SPARKS RUSH INTO GILTS AND STERLING

The announcement by chancellor Gordon Brown that the Bank of England will take responsibility for setting interest rates sparked a rush into gilts and sterling. UK government bond prices made their biggest one-day gains for over five years, with investors buoyed by expectations that the change will reduce long-term inflationary pressure in the economy. Sterling gained against both the Dollar and the Deutschemark, while the FT-SE 100 index closed up 63.7 at 4519.3.
-- BP HEAD GETS NEW TRADE POST

New prime minister Tony Blair is expected Wednesday to confirm the appointment of Sir David Simon, chairman of oil group BP, to a new ministerial job floating between the Department of Trade and Industry and the Treasury. The new full-time post, which will have a focus on trade promotion, also entails a peerage for Sir David, enabling him to act as spokesman for the Treasury in the House of Lords.
-- STRONG DEMAND SUPPORTS RATE RISE

The decision by the new government to raise interest base rates, to 6.25 per cent, has been justified by reports showing a booming service sector and strong demand in most regions of the UK. The monthly survey of service sector purchasing managers, published by the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply, reported strong growth last month. And a breakdown of regional activity in manufacturing, released by the Confederation of British Industry, also reported rising activity throughout much of the UK.
-- ENERGY USERS CALL FOR PRICES INQUIRY

John Battle, the new trade and industry minister with responsibility for energy, has been petitioned by big users of energy to launch an inquiry into pricing in the sector. The Energy Intensive Users Group called for a 'full review' of the Electricity Pool, the mechanism which administers the wholesale electricity market in England and Wales. According to the group, the Pool 'has not fostered competition in generation'.
-- CLUBS EXPECTED TO OPPOSE RADICAL PLAN FOR FOOTBALL

Some of the 72 clubs of the English Football League are expected Wednesday to oppose radical plans for a restructuring of the League. The plans are detailed in a report from consultants Deloitte & Touche, which includes proposals for regional leagues featuring more teams from the current (non-league) GM Vauxhall Conference. The aim of the report is to improve the poor financial state of most league clubs, of whom only 14 out of 72 are currently profitable.
-- WATER GROUPS FACE PRESSURE TO SHARE RESOURCES

Environment minister Michael Meacher has said the new government is planning tough action to force water companies which have surplus water to share it with those that are short. Such a move is likely to spark multi-million-pound compensation claims from the privatised water companies, which see their abstraction licences as precious assets. However, Meacher emphasised that despite the commercial interests, the public interest was of overriding concern to the government.
-- BSKB TO ORDER TV DECODERS

UK Satellite television company British Sky Broadcasting will begin ordering one million digital satellite decoders on from Panasonic, Amstrad, Pace Microelectronics and Hyundai in deals totalling over 300 million stg. The purchases further BSkyB's move into the advanced digital television market which will offer over 200 channels and a variety of interactive and specialty services. Decoders should be priced at around 200 pounds stg, with the launch expected in early 1998.
-- CAPITAL RADIO BUYS RIVAL VIRGIN IN 65 MILLION STG DEAL

Capital Radio has purchased three UK commercial radio stations from Richard Branson's Virgin Radio Group for 64.7 million stg in Capital shares. Branson commented that the sale was not a 'sell out', but a merger between the two groups, as Virgin will retain 14 per cent in the new Capital group and possibly acquire more in the future. The deal, yet to be approved, gives Capital 22 million stg in Virgin radio debt.
-- STERLING BOND ISSUE IS WORLD BANK'S BIGGEST

On Tuesday, the World Bank launched its biggest ever sterling denominated bond, at 750 million stg, over twice as large as its previous issue. Gumersindo Oliveros, senior manager in the treasury department at the World Bank said that the combination of chancellor Gordon Brown's interest rate announcement and rally in the glits market provided the 'ideal moment to issue the bond'.
